Select an actual URL from search results, fetch it, and retain its text and URL together. Reuse successful downloads from the original batch. edits.title: Record discoveries from inspected evidence without confusing verification with discovery
edits.content: Empty discovery placeholders previously caused stalled_search signals; later records do not erase earlier empty events. Inspect each search result group before recording discoveries, preserving search_many input order. If snippets lack names, distinguish that from an empty search: inspect the selected documents and attribute newly identified entities to their originating query before closing its discovery record. Keep a local ledger of entities and originating queries so names learned from fetched documents are not silently omitted from discovery bookkeeping. Record [] honestly for searches that only verify fields of already known entities; useful nationality or affiliation verification need not discover new people. Never invent discoveries or repeat known names merely to suppress a stall signal.

edits.title: Resolve semantic audit findings without narrowing the requested field
edits.content: A passing schema, quote-membership check, or constraint log does not establish semantic completeness. When an audit identifies additional historical affiliations or other omitted values, resolve the finding against the requested field definition and dated evidence. Do not dismiss concurrent or honorary affiliations solely because a preferred announcement omits them: 'affiliation at award' and 'affiliation listed by the awarding body' are different scopes. Verify whether the additional positions applied at the relevant date, then include supported values or document an evidence-based exclusion. An inconclusive follow-up search does not resolve the finding. Only mark the semantic constraint satisfied after this reconciliation.

decisions.reason: Reviewed all 29 occurrences. Signals 0–7 concern initial release searches whose snippets mostly lacked names; subsequent document extraction identified people, but discovery bookkeeping retained empty records. Signal 8 concerns a recovery search for already known people. Signals 9–17 and 18–27 concern nationality verification of an established roster, and signal 28 concerns affiliation verification; their empty discoveries are legitimate despite useful evidence gains. The existing memory correctly prohibits invented discoveries but does not explain attribution of document-derived names. Update it rather than treating every signal as failed research. The single recorded passing outcome does not justify deleting it.

All three failures recovered: the academy redirect loop was replaced by a discovered official PDF; the Axios 403 was followed by usable nationality profiles; the Princeton 403 was supplemented by fetched citizenship evidence elsewhere. Successful batch downloads were retained, with no repeated failing-fetch loop. The existing skill already captures alternate-source recovery and evidence validation, and its recorded outcome supplies no basis for deletion or another failure entry.

The audit reported concurrent affiliations supported by the supplied biography. The follow-up search did not resolve their historical applicability, yet the final code excluded other concurrent or honorary positions categorically and marked all constraints true. This supports a procedural memory about resolving scope and omissions, without prescribing any benchmark value. The self-check's coverage and verbatim successes do not settle that semantic question.

Programmatic checks found four affiliation quote mismatches, including column interleaving and whitespace problems. A prose reviewer incorrectly claimed two quotes already matched; official HTML patches subsequently passed literal validation. This confirms the existing skill's instruction to validate against exact downloaded text and use alternate formats. No separate edit is needed; the edit budget is better spent on discovery attribution and unresolved semantic auditing.
